If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 1.5–2.5% in mid-horizon (days 10–20) to avoid over-optimism.  
If sentiment is consistently negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 1.5–2.5% in early horizon (days 1–5) to compensate for downward bias.  
If sentiment swings sharply (≥0.33 to 1.00 or vice versa) within 3 days, adjust forecast slope downward by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon (days 20–30) to reflect volatility.  
If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and price is trending upward, add 0.5–1.0% to forecast in mid-horizon to capture momentum.  
If sentiment is neutral and price is trending downward, subtract 0.5–1.0% from forecast in mid-horizon to avoid overcorrection.  
If sentiment is positive but price is declining, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.0% in late horizon to align with sentiment divergence.
